subject: Re: DPA redlines — data geography & deletion windows
messages:
From: Samantha Jenkins <samantha.jenkins@arboryhealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Arbory Legal <legal@arboryhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redlines — data geography & deletion windows

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for sending the DPA. Our security and legal team reviewed and attached redlines (Arbory-DPA-redline.pdf). Key items we need clarification on before procurement can proceed:

- Onshore processing: For our EU customers, we require all processing (including backups and disaster recovery copies) to remain within the EU. Current DPA references "regional processing" but does not explicitly guarantee backups/restores will stay in-region.
- Deletion windows: We need customer-initiated erasure to be completed within 30 days for both primary stores and backups (or an explicit plan to purge backups within 30 days).
- KMS: Arbory requires the ability to control encryption keys for customer data (BYOK) for EU-based workloads.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II and most recent penetration test summary; for regulated customers we may request additional audit artifacts.

Can you confirm which of these Redwood can accept as-is, and where you will push back? We are on a tight timeline for our procurement (target signature 2027-04-29).

Appreciate a quick run-through so our procurement lead can move the contract forward.

Thanks,
Samantha
Director, Security & Compliance
Arbory Health

Attachment: Arbory-DPA-redline.pdf

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Jenkins <samantha.jenkins@arboryhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 13:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — data geography & deletion windows

Samantha — thanks, and appreciate the clear list. Looping Neha (Legal) and Karthik (Infra) so we can be precise. High-level responses below; I've attached a tracked-change counterproposal (RDW-counterproposal-track-changes.docx).

Summary of Redwood positions:
- Data geography: We can commit hosted production processing for EU customers to the eu-west-1 region. For Redwood Private/Dedicated (VPC or on-prem) customers, we support strict onshore-only processing.
- Backups & disaster recovery: For our hosted tier, backups are taken in-region where possible; however, depending on active failover and DR sites, we cannot guarantee physical media will never traverse to a second region without a specific contractual commitment and an associated architecture (additional charge).
- Deletion timelines: We can commit to logical deletion of customer data within 30 days of request for production stores. For backups we propose: logical deletion within 30 days; physical overwrite / secure wipe within 180 days (standard practice to account for backup rotation and integrity checks).
- KMS/BYOK: BYOK is supported for Redwood Private and Dedicated customers. For hosted customers we offer tenant-level keys in a Redwood-managed HSM; we can explore a cross-over arrangement (customer-managed keys for EU-hosted accounts) but that requires security review and an ops integration window.

Proposed clause language (suggested edits in attached doc):
"Redwood will process Customer Personal Data within the European Economic Area (EEA) for Customers that designate EU residency. Redwood will store and process Customer Personal Data in the eu-west-1 region, and will not transfer Customer Personal Data outside the EEA except as required to provide the Services or by applicable law.

Upon written request from Customer, Redwood will initiate logical deletion of Customer Personal Data from production systems within thirty (30) days. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to remove Customer Personal Data from backup media within one hundred eighty (180) days. For EU-only deployments (Dedicated or Private), Redwood will provide an option to contractually limit backup copies to EU-located infrastructure.
"

Neha/Karthik — can you review the backup wording and confirm if we can shorten the physical wipe window for EU-hosted customers under an add-on fee? My ask is: can we offer 90 days for EU-hosted as a compromise?

Samantha — I know the 180-day physical wipe may be longer than Arbory's standard. If you can share the exact regulatory citation requiring 30 days for backups, that will help us map a technical solution (e.g., Dedicated capacity or Private deployment with BYOK + EU-only backup cluster).

I can commit to providing SOC 2 Type II and our latest pen test summary for review. I'll follow up with the security pack in a separate email.

Best,
Priyom Das
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachment: RDW-counterproposal-track-changes.docx

From: Samantha Jenkins <samantha.jenkins@arboryhealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Arbory Legal <legal@arboryhealth.com>, Oliver Grant <oliver@legalops.co>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — data geography & deletion windows

Thanks Priyom — appreciate the quick turnaround and the doc. A couple of follow-ups from our side after an internal review:

- Regulator requirement: Our compliance team cites guidance that backups containing personal health information must be deletable within 30 days for certain data subject erasure requests (we can share the internal citation).
- 180 days for physical wipe is a non-starter for our procurement; we need a hard commit of 60 days or less on backup purge when data residency is EU. Otherwise our board will not approve hosted deployments.
- BYOK: BYOK for Private is fine, but Arbory is looking for a hosted option where the customer controls keys (we understand this is operationally heavier). Is Redwood willing to pilot tenant key management for eu-hosted production with appropriate SLA?

We are trying to avoid the Dedicated/Private route due to cost; the hosted option with stronger residency guarantees and BYOK would keep this in the deal. If you can move to 60 days for backup purge (or provide an expedited purge add-on that guarantees <30 days for EU customers), we can proceed to procurement and signature in two weeks. Please also attach SOC 2 Type II report and the pen test summary (redacted).

Thanks,
Samantha

Attachment: (Arbory internal citation will be shared in a follow-up)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Jenkins <samantha.jenkins@arboryhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 18:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — data geography & deletion windows

Samantha — thanks, quick update after syncing with Legal and Infra. We want to get Arbory over the finish line and have a commercially reasonable compromise that preserves security and our operational constraints. Proposed final position below (we've also attached an updated DPA PDF with edits: RDW-updated-DPA-20270416.pdf):

1) Residency and backups
- For eu-hosted customers, Redwood will ensure primary processing and primary data storage are located in eu-west-1.
- Redwood will, as part of a new EU Residency Addendum, offer an "EU-only backup" option for hosted customers. This option limits backups to EU-located infrastructure and requires a small monthly infrastructure premium.

2) Deletion timelines
- Logical deletion: Redwood will remove Customer Personal Data from production systems within thirty (30) days of a valid erasure request.
- Backups: For customers on the standard hosted plan, Redwood will remove Customer Personal Data from backup media within ninety (90) days.
- Expedited purge add-on: For customers selecting the EU-only backup option (or via a one-time expedited purge fee), Redwood will commit to removing Customer Personal Data from backup media within thirty (30) days of request. This is a firm SLA tied to the add-on.

3) Keys and encryption
- BYOK: Redwood supports BYOK for Dedicated and Private deployments. For eu-hosted customers, Redwood will run a pilot to enable customer-managed keys (tenant-level keys) for accounts where Arbory agrees to a short integration and security assessment period. The pilot will be contractually scoped and timeboxed.

4) Evidence and audits
- Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II report and a redacted penetration test summary. For customers requiring deeper audits, Redwood offers an on-site or remote audit option under mutual NDA and reasonable scheduling windows.

If this compromise is acceptable, next steps:
- Arbory confirms acceptance of the EU-only backup add-on or expedited purge fee model so we can attach pricing.
- Neha will finalize the DPA edits and produce a DocuSign-ready PDF (link above).
- We will include language to operationalize the 30-day expedited purge and the pilot BYOK agreement.

Neha: please review and confirm the DPA wording in RDW-updated-DPA-20270416.pdf. Karthik: please confirm that an expedited purge within 30 days is operationally achievable for EU-only backup sets (and note any cost/availability constraints).

Samantha — happy to hop on a 30-minute call today if helpful to close this.

Best regards,
Priyom Das
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachments: RDW-updated-DPA-20270416.pdf
